0.0.n: This is the Japanese name for the United Kingdom.

0.1.n: Marks the place where she was born.

0.2.n: The connecting form of 生まれる links her birth to the next event.

0.4.n: Describes her age during the time indicated by ころ.

0.5.n: Follows 幼い to refer to the time when she was young.

0.6.n: This country name gives the destination of her move.

0.7.n: Marks the destination of 移住した.

0.8.n: The past form of 移住する describes relocating to another country or region.

0.10.n: This is the first portion of the personal name Olivia Newton-John.

0.12.n: This completes Newton-John, her hyphenated surname; it is not a separate person's name.

0.13.n: A respectful title attached to a person's name, commonly used in news reports.

1.0.n: 年 marks this number as a calendar year.

1.1.n: Marks the year when her debut took place.

1.2.n: Placed before デビュー, this identifies the profession in which she debuted.

1.3.n: The connecting form of デビューする lets the account continue into the next line.

2.1.n: Part of the Japanese song title for Have You Never Been Mellow.

2.2.n: Links そよ風 to 誘惑 within the song title.

2.3.n: Completes the Japanese song title, literally meaning a gentle breeze's temptation.

2.6.n: This is the song title written in katakana.

2.8.n: Indicates that the two named songs are examples, not a complete list.

2.9.n: Connects the listed examples with ヒット曲, identifying them as hit songs.

2.10.n: Combines ヒット with 曲, the word for a song or musical piece.

2.11.n: Marks the hit songs as the means through which she earned awards.

2.13.n: Used with の to emphasize the large number of awards.

2.14.n: Links 数々 to 賞, forming a phrase describing many awards.

2.15.n: Japanese does not require a plural ending; 数々 makes the quantity clear.

2.16.n: Pairs 賞 with 輝き in an expression meaning to win awards.

2.17.n: The connecting form of 輝く, literally to shine, means winning honors when used with 賞に.

3.0.n: This word can refer to performers of any gender.

3.1.n: Marks the professional role in which she also achieved success.

3.2.n: Adds acting to her previously mentioned singing career.

3.4.n: This is the given name of actor John Travolta.

3.6.n: This is only the first segment of トラボルタ, the surname Travolta, not an independent word.

3.7.n: This completes トラボルタ, the surname Travolta; the subtitle splits the name into two segments.

3.8.n: A respectful title attached to John Travolta's full name.

3.9.n: Introduces the person who shared the starring role with her.

3.10.n: The past form of 主演する modifies 映画, specifying the film in which she starred.

3.11.n: The preceding description identifies her role, and the following title names the movie.

3.13.n: This is the film's title, written in katakana.

3.15.n: Marks the movie as the subject of 大ヒットする; it has no separate English equivalent here.

3.16.n: The nonpast form 大ヒットする appears inside a historical example; the final verb places the account in the past.

3.17.n: Presents the film's success as one example of her achievements.

4.0.n: The ending 的 turns 世界 into a description of international scope.

4.1.n: This borrowed word refers to a famous entertainer.

4.2.n: Marks the resulting status with なる, using a more formal alternative to に.

4.3.n: The polite past form of なる concludes the account of her rise to fame.

0.lit: Born in Britain, moved to Australia when young, Ms. Olivia Newton-John.
0.tip: Japanese can place a long description before a person's name, as it does here.

1.lit: In 1966, made her singer debut, and…
1.tip: The ending し connects デビューする to the continuing account rather than ending the sentence.

2.lit: With hit songs such as Gentle Breeze's Temptation and Physical, shone in numerous awards, and…
2.tip: 賞に輝く literally evokes shining, but means winning an award.

3.lit: Also as an actor, the film Grease, in which she starred together with Mr. John Travolta, became a huge hit.
3.tip: 主演した modifies 映画 directly, doing the work of English in which she starred.

4.tip: と marks what she became; スターとなる is a more formal alternative to スターになる.
